origin.description: Count the Unicode code points in each string. Those are the pieces str_sub can extract.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

origin.details: The count is code points, not the number of columns used when the string is printed. A missing string stays missing. Names on string are copied onto the result. NULL is an empty integer vector.
origin.value: An integer vector the same length as string.
origin.example:
x <- str_length(c("i", "like", "programming", NA))
u <- str_length(c("\u00fc", "u\u0308"))
cat(paste0("str_length(c(\"i\", \"like\", \"programming\", NA)) returns ", paste(ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", x), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_length of u-umlaut and u plus accent returns ", paste(u, collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Count the Unicode code points in each string by calling stringi.stri_length.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, a number, a logical, or a list of those. None is an empty vector. A bare string has length 1.

translation.details: The result is always a list. Character NA is stringi._na.NA, and the letters NA have length 2. Names stored on the input are copied when the lengths match. A factor in R is coerced with as.character before the count; pass the label string here.
translation.value: A list of ints the same length as string. A missing string is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringr.length import str_length
x = str_length(["i", "like", "programming", NA])
u = str_length(["\u00fc", "u\u0308"])
shown = ", ".join("NA" if item is NA else str(item) for item in x)
print(f"str_length([\"i\", \"like\", \"programming\", NA]) returns {shown}.")
print("str_length of u-umlaut and u plus accent returns " + ", ".join(str(item) for item in u) + ".")
